Let's analyze the exact output from the Moon page search: 1. `| periapsis = {{gaps |362 |600}} km
({{gaps |356 |400}}–{{gaps |370 |400}} km)` 2. `between {{convert|356,400|km|mi|abbr=on}} ([[perigee]])` So the minimum perigee value on the Wikipedia page for the Moon is **356,400 km**. Now let's examine Kipchoge's record marathon pace. Let's check Kipchoge's marathon world record times: - World record set in 2022: 2 hours 1 minute 9 seconds (2:01:09). - World record set in 2018: 2 hours 1 minute 39 seconds (2:01:39). - Sub-two-hour exhibition in 2019: 1 hour 59 minutes 40.2 seconds (1:59:40). Let's write a python script to calculate the speed and the time to cover 356,400 km for all these cases (and any other potential values/interpretations), and check the rounded results in thousand hours! ```python cmd = """python3 -c " distance_km = 356400 marathon_km = 42.195 # Times in seconds times = { '2:01:09 (2022 WR)': 2*3600 + 1*60 + 9, '2:01:39 (2018 WR)': 2*3600 + 1*60 + 39, '1:59:40 (INEOS 1:59)': 1*3600 + 59*60 + 40, '1:59:40.2 (INEOS exact)': 1*3600 + 59*60 + 40.2, } for label, t_sec in times.items(): speed_km_s = marathon_km / t_sec speed_km_h = speed_km_s * 3600 time_hours = distance_km / speed_km_h time_k_hours = time_hours / 1000 rounded_k_hours = round(time_k_hours) rounded_nearest_1000_hours = round(time_hours, -3) print(f'{label}:') print(f' Speed: {speed_km_h:.6f} km/h') print(f' Time in hours: {time_hours:.3f}') print(f' In thousand hours: {time_k_hours:.3f} k-hours') print(f' Rounded to nearest 1000 hours: {rounded_nearest_1000_hours:.0f}') print(f' Thousands value: {rounded_k_hours}') " """ out = await run_command(cmd) print(out) ```
